sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sceolan was an Irish mythological beast. He was one of the hunting hounds of Fionn mac Cumhaill. His story turns on shape-shifting. Sceolan would have been human except that his mother, Uirne, had been bewitched into canine form. She was later restored to human form, but her twin pups Sceolan and Bran stayed in their dog bodies. Their uncle, the hero Fionn, made both dogs part of the Fianna, his band of warriors. There they gave good service as hunters, fighters, and sentinels. Sceolan took his place in the band of warriors and became a beast of the hunt in the service of the great hero. The tale ties a dog's loyalty to the world of Fionn and the Fianna.
objective: Document the Irish mythological beast Sceolan.
